newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Brcko will be decided without Serbs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Brcko will be decided without Serbs.

text.p: The United States on Monday warned Bosnian Serbs who have pulled out of arbitration over the strategically important town of Brcko that the dispute would be settled without them.
The Serbs announced their withdrawal on Sunday, accusing the U.S. representative on the arbitration panel, Roberts Owen, of trying to impose a solution that favoured Bosnia's Moslems and Croats.

Brcko sits astride a strip of land in northern Bosnia linking the two halves of the Serbs' Republika Srpska. Last year's Dayton accord which ended the Bosnia war appointed a three-man panel to determine the town's status.

"The message to the Bosnian Serbs who are attempting to pull out is the following: With or without their direct participation in the arbitration proceedings, the arbitration tribunal for Brcko will reach a decision," a State Department spokesman said.
"The Bosnian Serbs are obligated under the Dayton agreement to accept and implement the independent decision that the arbitration panel ... will make," spokesman Nicholas Burns told a news briefing.

"The Serbs will have to live with the decisions of the Brcko arbitration panel. They have no choice in this matter. They signed on the dotted line and they're going to have to comply with that commitment," Burns added.
Apart from Owen, the panel consisted of a Serb and a representative of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation. Dayton divided Bosnia roughly equally between the Federation and the Republika Srpska.
